charnia: A Charnia, an Ediacaran ANIMAL, tall and narrow and feather-shaped: a slender upright stem widening into a long pointed blade built of MANY SMALL IDENTICAL QUILTED SEGMENTS ARRANGED IN TWO ALTERNATING ROWS up either side of a central midline, each segment a soft padded ridge. Anchored below by a small round holdfast disc. Soft pale grey-brown. An animal, absolutely NOT a plant and NOT a fern.
dickinsonia: A Dickinsonia, an Ediacaran animal shaped as a FLAT LOW OVAL, wider than it is thick and lying face-up, its whole surface divided into MANY FINE PARALLEL RIBBED SEGMENTS running out from a central line to the rim, the segments slightly OFFSET rather than matching across the midline. Broad at one end and tapering at the other. Soft, low and quilted, warm grey-brown.
anomalocaris: An Anomalocaris, a large Cambrian swimming predator with a segmented tubular body edged along both sides by a ROW OF OVERLAPPING FLEXIBLE SWIMMING FLAPS like a fringe of paddles. At the front, TWO LARGE SPINY SEGMENTED GRASPING APPENDAGES curve down and inward beneath a circular plated mouth, and TWO BIG COMPOUND EYES stand out on short stalks. A fan of blades at the tail.
opabinia: An Opabinia, a small Cambrian animal with a soft segmented body edged in side flaps, and two features that identify it: FIVE STALKED EYES ON TOP OF ITS HEAD, and a SINGLE LONG FLEXIBLE HOSE-LIKE NOZZLE projecting forward from the front of the head, ending in a small toothed grasping claw. Soft pale orange-brown, with a small fan of blades at the tail.
hallucigenia: A Hallucigenia, a tiny worm-like Cambrian animal with a long tubular body, walking on SEVEN PAIRS OF SLENDER CLAWED LEGS BENEATH, while SEVEN PAIRS OF LONG STIFF SHARP SPINES STAND STRAIGHT UP FROM ITS BACK in matching pairs. At one end a small simple head with two tiny eyespots and a ring of fine teeth. Pale cream and rust.
pneumodesmus: A Pneumodesmus, a VERY SMALL early millipede only about a centimetre long, with a long narrow segmented body of many short identical armoured rings, each ring carrying a pair of tiny legs beneath, and a small blunt head with short antennae. Its shell is finely textured, dull olive-brown.
cameroceras: A Cameroceras, an enormous ancient nautiloid with a STRAIGHT CONICAL SHELL, narrow at the point and widening evenly to a broad open mouth, several times longer than the animal itself and divided across by MANY FINE EVENLY SPACED CURVED CHAMBER LINES. From the wide open end emerges a squid-like head with large eyes and a crown of stout tentacles.
jaekelopterus: A Jaekelopterus, a giant sea scorpion AS LONG AS A PERSON IS TALL, with a broad shield-shaped head plate, a long tapering segmented body ending in a narrow spike, and TWO ENORMOUS FORWARD-REACHING CLAWED ARMS carrying long curved spines along their inner edges. Its rear pair of legs are flattened into broad swimming paddles. Glossy dark chestnut-brown.
dunkleosteus: A Dunkleosteus, a huge armoured fish whose entire head and shoulders are encased in THICK INTERLOCKING BONY PLATES like riveted armour, ending abruptly where the bare muscular body begins. It has NO TEETH: instead the plates themselves are drawn out into LONG SELF-SHARPENING BONY SHEARING BLADES along the jaw edges. Small eyes ringed by a bony collar.
tiktaalik: A Tiktaalik, a flat-headed fish shaped like the first step onto land: a broad FLATTENED CROCODILE-LIKE HEAD with eyes on TOP, a body still covered in overlapping scales and ending in a fish's tail fin, and STOUT MUSCULAR FRONT FINS carrying real shoulder, elbow and wrist joints, propping the front of the body up. It HAS A NECK, so the head turns independently of the body.
ichthyostega: An Ichthyostega, an early four-limbed animal built like a heavy salamander: a broad flat head, a barrel chest with STOUT SPRAWLING LIMBS held out sideways, overlapping bony ribs forming a broad basket, and a TAIL THAT IS STILL A FISH'S TAIL, flattened and edged with a fringe of fin rays. Dark olive skin, smooth and damp.
meganeura: A Meganeura, a giant ancient dragonfly-like insect with a WINGSPAN AS WIDE AS A PERSON'S OUTSTRETCHED ARMS: four long narrow stiff wings held out straight and flat, finely veined and faintly amber, a very long slender segmented abdomen, a small head almost entirely taken up by TWO ENORMOUS COMPOUND EYES, and six spiny legs held forward in a basket.
arthropleura: An Arthropleura, a giant millipede AS LONG AS A CAR, its body a long series of MANY BROAD FLAT OVERLAPPING ARMOURED PLATES, each plate wider than it is long and flaring out at the sides into blunt points, with a small rounded head at the front. Dozens of short sturdy legs run in rows beneath. Dark olive and rust brown, faintly glossy.
dimetrodon: A Dimetrodon, a sprawling four-legged predator that is NOT A DINOSAUR: a heavy lizard-shaped body with limbs held out to the sides, a large deep skull with teeth of TWO DISTINCT SIZES including long stabbing front fangs, and A TALL SAIL RUNNING DOWN ITS BACK, built of long bony spines with skin stretched between them, taller than the animal is deep.
gorgonops: A Gorgonops, a powerful four-legged predator with a MAMMAL-LIKE UPRIGHT STANCE, its legs held more under the body than out to the sides. Its long deep skull carries A PAIR OF LONG CURVED SABRE CANINES in the upper jaw projecting below the lip, small eyes set high, and it has bare leathery greyish skin. Absolutely NOT a dinosaur and NOT a cat.
elrathia: An Elrathia, a SMALL trilobite about the length of a thumbnail, seen from above: an oval armoured shell divided lengthwise into THREE CLEAR LOBES, a broad smooth semicircular head shield with a raised central dome and small crescent eyes, a middle section of about a dozen jointed ribbed segments, and a smooth rounded tail shield. Warm grey-brown.
megalodon: A Megalodon, an enormous stocky shark built much heavier and thicker through the body than a modern great white, with a SHORT BROAD BLUNT SNOUT, a very wide gaping mouth carrying rows of ENORMOUS BROAD TRIANGULAR SERRATED TEETH each as large as a hand, small eyes, huge stiff pointed pectoral fins and a tall crescent tail. Slate grey above, pale below.
basilosaurus: A Basilosaurus, an ancient whale with an EXTREMELY LONG SLENDER SERPENTINE BODY, many times longer than it is thick, undulating in a slow curve. It has a long narrow crocodile-like skull with pointed cutting teeth, small front flippers, a TINY PAIR OF USELESS HIND LEGS the size of a hand near the back of the body, and a small tail fluke. Dark grey-brown.
ambulocetus: An Ambulocetus, an early whale that still walks: a long low-slung heavy-bodied furred mammal with a LONG NARROW SNOUT full of pointed teeth, small eyes set high on the skull, SHORT POWERFUL LEGS ENDING IN BROAD SPLAYED PADDLE-LIKE FEET, and a long thick muscular tail. Coarse dark brown fur.
sinosauropteryx: A Sinosauropteryx, a small two-legged feathered dinosaur about the size of a turkey, its whole body covered in a coat of SIMPLE HAIR-LIKE BRISTLY FILAMENTS rather than flat feathers. Its known colours: GINGER-CHESTNUT ALONG THE BACK, pale cream below, a DARK BANDIT MASK ACROSS THE EYES, and a LONG TAIL RINGED WITH ALTERNATING GINGER AND WHITE BANDS. Small arms, long legs.
gigantopithecus: A Gigantopithecus, an enormous extinct ape built far heavier than a gorilla, with a MASSIVE DEEP JAW AND BROAD FLAT MOLAR TEETH, a low forehead, a wide flaring cheekbone on each side, and small eyes set deep. Its body is thickset with heavy shoulders and long arms, covered in coarse shaggy red-brown hair. Standing on all fours.
